claim: The legislature convenes in regular session on the first Tuesday after the second Monday in January of each odd-numbered year
quote: The legislature shall meet at the seat of government on the first Tuesday after the second Monday in January of each odd-numbered year.

claim: The regular session may not run past the first Monday after the third Saturday in May
quote: after the first Monday following the third Saturday in May of any year

claim: The regular session meets each biennium at times prescribed by law, for at most 120 legislative days
quote: in regular session in each biennium at the times prescribed by law for not exceeding a total of 120 legislative days

claim: Most new laws take effect on 1 August after final enactment unless the act says otherwise
quote: takes effect on August 1 next following its final enactment, unless a different date is specified in the act

claim: City general elections are held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even-numbered years by default
quote: The municipal general election in each city shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in every even-numbered year.

claim: A city may move its election to odd-numbered years by ordinance, but not hold elections in both
quote: A city may hold elections in either the even-numbered year or the odd-numbered year, but not both.

claim: The ordinance moving the election year must pass at least 180 days before filing opens
quote: by ordinance passed at a regular meeting held at least 180 calendar days before the first day to file for candidacy in the next municipal election

claim: Voters can force a referendum on an ordinance changing the city election year
quote: a petition requesting a referendum on the ordinance may be filed with the city clerk

claim: Chapter 205's election rules apply to both statutory and home rule charter cities, apart from listed sections a charter may replace
quote: In all statutory and home rule charter cities, the primary, general and special elections held for choosing city officials and deciding public questions relating to the city shall be held as provided in this chapter

claim: A home rule charter controls nominations, primaries and elections for city offices even where it conflicts with general law
quote: shall control as to nominations, primary elections, and elections for municipal offices, notwithstanding that such charter provisions may be inconsistent with any general law relating thereto

claim: A city primary is optional, held on the second Tuesday in August when the city has chosen to nominate by primary
quote: elect to choose nominees for municipal offices by a primary as provided in this section

claim: The city primary date is the second Tuesday in August of a city election year
quote: may be held in any city on the second Tuesday in August of any year in which a municipal general election is to be held

claim: City primary candidates appear without party labels
quote: The clerk shall place upon the primary ballot without partisan designation the names of individuals whose candidacies have been filed

claim: The top two per seat advance from a city primary and appear on the general ballot without party labels
quote: place them on the municipal general election ballot without partisan designation

claim: If no more than twice as many candidates file as there are seats, no city primary is held for that office
quote: their names shall not be placed upon the primary ballot and shall be placed on the municipal general election ballot as the nominees for that office

claim: Judicial, county, municipal, school district and special district offices are nonpartisan offices
quote: means all judicial, county, municipal, school district, and special district offices

claim: Partisan offices are federal, constitutional and legislative offices only
quote: means federal offices, presidential electors, constitutional offices, and legislative offices

claim: In election law a municipality is a city or a town (township)
quote: means any city or town

claim: Town general elections are held on the second Tuesday in March unless the town has moved them
quote: The general election in a town must be held on the second Tuesday in March

claim: A town may move its election to November of an even or odd year
quote: designate the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of either the even-numbered or the odd-numbered year as the date of the town general election

claim: Moving a town election to November needs a vote of the town's electors
quote: is effective upon an affirmative vote of the electors at the next town general election

claim: School district general elections are held in November of either odd or even years
quote: The general election in each school district must be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of either the odd-numbered or the even-numbered year.

claim: A school board may change its election year by resolution
quote: The school board may, by resolution, change the year in which the school district general election will be held.

claim: A school board primary is held only if the board has chosen to nominate by primary
quote: decide to choose nominees for school board by a primary as provided in this section

claim: School board candidates appear without party labels
quote: place them on the school district general election ballot without partisan designation

claim: An independent school district board has six elected members on four-year terms
quote: The membership of the board shall consist of six elected directors

claim: School board members serve four-year terms
quote: The term of office of a member shall be four years commencing on the first Monday in January

claim: Voters may enlarge a school board to seven members
quote: the question whether the board shall consist of seven members

claim: The state primary is held on the second Tuesday in August of even-numbered years and nominates nonpartisan offices on the state general ballot
quote: The state primary shall be held on the second Tuesday in August in each even-numbered year

claim: The state general election, which carries county offices, is in November of even-numbered years
quote: The state general election shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in each even-numbered year.

claim: Nonpartisan offices are dropped from the primary when no more than twice as many candidates file as there are seats
quote: their names and the name of the office shall be omitted from the state and county nonpartisan primary ballot

claim: The top two in a county or other nonpartisan primary advance to November
quote: receiving the highest and the next highest number of votes shall be the nominees for that office

claim: At the state partisan primary a voter may vote in only one party's column
quote: permits you to vote for the candidates of only one political party in a state partisan primary election

claim: A partisan primary ballot marked for more than one party is not counted on the partisan section
quote: the ballot is totally defective and no vote on the partisan section of the ballot shall be counted

claim: Election judges may not record which party a voter belongs to or voted for
quote: showing the political party to which a voter belongs or for which political party the voter voted

claim: The presidential nomination primary is the exception: the party ballot a voter requests is recorded
quote: the election judge must record in the polling place roster the name of the political party whose ballot the voter requested

claim: Nobody can be nominated by petition for a nonpartisan office
quote: No individual shall be nominated by nominating petition for any nonpartisan office.

claim: Nominating petitions are the route for partisan-office candidates who are not seeking a major party nomination
quote: Candidates for any partisan office who do not seek the nomination of a major political party shall be nominated by nominating petition

claim: Only voters eligible to vote for the candidate may sign a nominating petition
quote: A nominating petition may be signed only by individuals who are eligible to vote for the candidate who is nominated.

claim: A voter may not sign petitions for more candidates for one office than there are seats
quote: No individual may sign more than one nominating petition for candidates for the same office unless more than one candidate is to be elected to that office.

claim: A candidate may file a petition instead of paying the filing fee
quote: At the time of filing an affidavit of candidacy, a candidate may present a petition in place of the filing fee.

claim: City candidates file an affidavit of candidacy with the municipal clerk
quote: shall file an affidavit of candidacy with the municipal clerk

claim: County offices are won by plurality: the candidate with the most votes is declared elected
quote: declare the candidate duly elected who received the highest number of votes for each county and state office voted for only within the county

claim: Hospital district boards declare the highest vote-getter elected
quote: declare the candidate duly elected who received the highest number of votes for each hospital district office

claim: Each county has a five-member board of commissioners on four-year terms by default
quote: Each county shall have a board of five commissioners who shall be known as the county board and whose terms of office shall be four years

claim: Anoka, Hennepin, Ramsey and St. Louis counties have seven-member boards
quote: In Anoka, Hennepin, Ramsey, and St. Louis Counties the board shall have seven members.

claim: Any county may change its board to three, five, seven or nine members
quote: Any county may provide that the board of county commissioners shall consist of three, five, seven or nine members.

claim: Counties with 100,000 or more people may move to a seven-member board by resolution
quote: Any county with a population of 100,000 or more according to the last federal decennial census may by resolution of its county board provide for a seven-member board of county commissioners.

claim: Commissioners are elected one per district and must live in the district
quote: One commissioner shall be elected in each district who, at the time of the election, is a resident of the district.

claim: Counties elect an auditor, treasurer, sheriff, recorder and county attorney to four-year terms unless an office has been combined or made appointive
quote: a county auditor, a county treasurer, sheriff, county recorder, county attorney, and coroner

claim: Elected county offices can be consolidated or made appointive
quote: unless an office is consolidated with another county office or made appointive under chapter 375A or other general or special law

claim: A county board may make the auditor, treasurer or recorder appointive
quote: A county board may appoint the county auditor, county treasurer, or county recorder

claim: The optional forms chapter does not apply to Hennepin County
quote: This chapter does not apply to Hennepin County.

claim: The staggered-term rule for new or enlarged county boards does not apply to Ramsey County
quote: This section does not apply to Ramsey County.

claim: A local government may adopt a home rule charter only when authorized by law
quote: Any local government unit when authorized by law may adopt a home rule charter for its government.

claim: Ramsey County has a special law authorizing a county charter commission
quote: the Ramsey County legislative delegation means all elected members of the state house of representatives and state senate whose legislative district includes a portion of Ramsey County

claim: Ramsey County's charter may provide for new elective or appointive officers
quote: It shall provide for present functions to be assumed by new elective or appointive officers as shall be provided for in the charter

claim: County boards may create election precincts for unorganized territory
quote: A county board may establish new election precincts to serve the residents of unorganized territories.

claim: Towns elect three supervisors to three-year terms by default
quote: Each supervisor shall be elected for a term of three years

claim: Towns elect three supervisors at the town general election
quote: three supervisors shall be elected in each town at the town general election

claim: Towns that vote in November elect their officers to four-year terms
quote: supervisors and other town officers in towns that hold the town general election in November shall be elected for terms of four years

claim: A November town may move supervisors to six-year terms
quote: may adopt a resolution establishing six-year terms for supervisors

claim: Towns elect a clerk and a treasurer on two-year terms unless the offices have been made appointive or combined
quote: The clerk and treasurer each shall serve for two years and until their successors are elected and qualified.

claim: A town may adopt a five-member board
quote: A town may provide for a five-member board of supervisors

claim: A town may make its clerk and treasurer appointed by the town board
quote: A town may provide for the appointment by the town board of its clerk or treasurer, or both

claim: Every city without a home rule charter is a statutory city, including every former village
quote: the term includes every city which was a village on January 1, 1974

claim: The term village is no longer applied to statutory cities
quote: shall not be applied to any municipal corporation operating under the authority of this chapter

claim: Villages, boroughs and non-charter cities were brought under one statutory city code in 1973-74
quote: bringing the basic laws relating to all villages, boroughs and cities without home rule charters under a single code of statutes

claim: A statutory city is one that has not adopted a home rule charter
quote: means any city which has not adopted a home rule charter pursuant to the constitution and laws

claim: Any city may frame a home rule charter, with no population threshold
quote: Any city in the state may frame a city charter for its own government

claim: A home rule charter must provide for a mayor and an elected council
quote: provide for a mayor, and for a council to be elected by the people

claim: A charter chooses the form of government and whether officers are elected at large or otherwise
quote: may provide that all elective city officers, including mayor and members of the council, shall be elected at large or otherwise

claim: City classes are by population and exist for legislative purposes
quote: Cities are hereby divided, for legislative purposes, into classes as follows

claim: A first class city keeps its class unless its population falls 25 percent
quote: it shall not be reclassified unless its population decreases by 25 percent from the census figures which last qualified the city for inclusion in the class

claim: Under the standard plan, voters elect the mayor, council members, the clerk and the treasurer if there is one
quote: the voters elect the treasurer, if there is one, and a council consisting of a mayor, three or five council members, and the clerk or clerk-treasurer

claim: Optional Plan A makes the clerk and treasurer appointed
quote: Any statutory city may provide for the appointment of its clerk and treasurer

claim: Optional Plan B is the council-manager plan, open to statutory cities over 1,000 people
quote: Any statutory city of more than 1,000 population may provide for the council-manager plan of government

claim: A Plan B council is a mayor and four or six council members
quote: be composed of a mayor and four or six council members

claim: A statutory city council may set a two- or four-year mayoral term by ordinance
quote: The council may, by ordinance, establish a four-year term or reestablish a two-year term for the office of mayor

claim: Voters may enlarge or shrink a statutory city council to seven or five
quote: the question of whether the city council should be increased or reduced to seven or five members

claim: A statutory city may elect its council by ward
quote: A city may adopt an ordinance to elect its city council members by ward

claim: Soil and water conservation district supervisors are elected at the state general election with no primary
quote: Elections must be held at the state general election specified in section 204D.03, subdivision 2 . A primary may not be held.

claim: Soil and water supervisors are nominated by supervisor district but elected at large
quote: one or more supervisors shall be nominated from each supervisor district

claim: A hospital district board has one member from each city and town in the district plus one at large
quote: composed of one member elected from each city and town in the district and one member elected at large
